sampling_model.design: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections at a common baseline and dates \(1,\ldots,T\), with cohort \(g\) treated from date \(g\) onward.
sampling_model.units: Independent Gaussian cohort-time cell means with known variance \(\sigma^2/(Nq_g)\) at each wave.
sampling_model.treatment: For each \(t\le T-m\), cohort \(g\le t\) is compared with pooled set \(C_t\); no untreated cohort remains for the target at \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed shares satisfy \(c_q/T\le q_g\le C_q/T\), and \(q_{>t}>0\) at every score date.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated inside the exact known-covariance Gaussian score experiment. Holder calendar paths and bounded centered cohort deviations define the law class; no bounded-lift or calendar-rate equivalence is imposed as an assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 3.3, Proposition 5, shows that sufficiently long-run nonnegative weighted effects are not identified without extrapolation when no never-treated units remain.
The paper identifies group-time ATTs, defines calendar aggregations, and provides simultaneous inference for identified collections.
Proposition 1 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function and its efficiency bound for the two-period ATT.
Gaussian linear-functional difficulty is characterized through a modulus, and affine minimax rules are near global minimax rules.
Known-variance Gaussian confidence procedures over convex regression classes are characterized by ordered moduli and sharp expected-length bounds.
Theorem 3.1 on pp. 15--16 derives a simple honest interval and its Holder boundary bias--variance calibration for nonparametric regression.
Uniformly valid DiD confidence sets are constructed under bounded post-treatment deviations from observed pre-trends.
Loewner covariance dominance and Anderson's theorem order Gaussian procedures for symmetric convex acceptance regions.

body.tldr: A fixed-cohort repeated-cross-section event study induces an exact Gaussian not-yet-treated score experiment with shrinking control pools and nested shared-baseline covariance. The contribution is now stated at the operator-specific frontier that is proved: global minimax MSE is bounded above and below by explicit constants times \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2\), and measurable uniformly honest intervals have expected length bounded by explicit constants times \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\). A new equal-share obstruction theorem shows that the proposed separate Holder-leverage, cohort-deviation-leverage, and \(O(T/k^2)\) baseline-energy certificate cannot hold at \(m=1\), \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). The matched-date-block calculation remains an exact marginal diagnostic for \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\) only. Converting the exact nested modulus to a closed-form calendar rate remains open.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD methods diagnose the loss of valid late comparisons, while Gaussian optimal-recovery theory starts from a supplied operator and covariance. Neither literature derives the nested shared-baseline covariance of these not-yet-treated scores or determines how that covariance obstructs a natural calendar-rate certificate.
project_justification.niche: The causal design creates a finite but growing Gaussian inverse problem in which the same baseline cells couple all comparison dates. This operator admits exact modulus-based risk and honest-length analysis, yet its baseline Gram term prevents a tempting datewise information argument.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the nested covariance, proves an equal-share baseline-energy obstruction for the proposed four-part dual certificate, constructs total measurable modulus estimators and bias-aware intervals, and matches their global MSE and honest expected length to the exact nested modulus with explicit constants. The closed-form calendar conversion is isolated as an open problem rather than claimed.

body.related_work: Callaway and Sant'Anna supply the group-time effects and calendar aggregation that give the target its causal interpretation. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess show in Section 3.3, Proposition 5, why long-run event-study effects lose valid comparisons, motivating explicit extrapolation. Sant'Anna and Zhao give a two-period repeated-cross-section efficiency benchmark, whereas the covariance lemma here derives the growing-calendar nested score law. Donoho's 1994 model (equation (1)), Theorem 1, and Section 11 provide Gaussian modulus machinery conditional on a supplied operator. Armstrong and Kolesar's 2018 Section 3.2, equations (23)--(26), and their 2020 equation (15) and Theorem 3.1 on pp. 15--16 provide bias-aware Gaussian interval and Holder-regression calibrations conditional on supplied weights. None supplies a bounded right inverse for the staggered-DiD baseline Gram term. The new contribution is therefore the design-derived nested covariance, the operator-specific baseline-energy obstruction, and the exact-modulus consequences; the matched-date-block calculation is supporting calibration only and does not transfer its rate to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\). Rambachan and Roth concern sensitivity to trend violations rather than bounded treatment-effect heterogeneity, and Cohen and Fogarty motivate covariance-order diagnostics without implying an ordering here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The obstruction theorem rules out the proposed four-separate-inequality dual certificate uniformly at equal shares, \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\); it does not prove that every bounded lift is impossible and does not prove that the exact nested modulus is or is not comparable to the candidate calendar diagnostic. The matched comparison deletes only cross-date dependence while preserving each full within-date covariance block, so its finite information sum and homogeneous Holder rate apply only to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\). Equal block marginals do not order the nested and block-diagonal experiments. Non-Gaussian coupling and nuisance estimation remain outside the exact score experiment.
body.honest_scope: The proved headline consists of the exact nested score covariance, the equal-share baseline-covariance certificate obstruction, explicit-constant global minimax MSE bounds in terms of \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\), and exact-coverage bias-aware intervals whose shortest honest expected length is bounded by explicit constants times the same modulus. The interval lower bound ranges over measurable interval-valued procedures. No phase diagram or closed-form nested calendar rate is claimed. The diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), its minimizing depth, smoothness adaptation, and any equivalence between that diagnostic and the exact modulus remain open. Generic Gaussian modulus theory and the matched-date-block calculation are supporting ingredients rather than novelty claims.
body.interpretation: The exact modulus \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) is computable from the finite-dimensional convex program defined by the observed score operator, the known nested covariance, and the Holder-plus-bounded-cohort class. It is the proved difficulty scale for both point estimation and honest intervals. The candidate \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) remains useful for diagnosing three intuitive calendar components, but its minimizer \(k^\star\) is not established as an oracle depth for the nested experiment. The obstruction identifies the shared baseline, rather than contemporaneous date-block noise, as the precise failure of the proposed separate dual bounds.
